text:
Liam: Heads-up: canary ran into a cold-start spike for a model using delta-sidecar shards. First-request latency jumped ~2.5x.
Rosa: Which model bundle?
Liam: s3://redwood-canary/deltas/exp-2025-02-11/{sha}.safetensors + sidecar .delta (zstd delta stream).
kyle: Interesting. Does loader apply delta patch before warmup? I think our warmup assumes final tensor layout available on disk.
Yuki: Confirmed in local repro: our warmup path tries to map tensor offsets to precomputed index, but sidecar deltas change byte offsets until applied. Warmup aborted -> fallback to streaming reads.
Priya: Two options: 1) apply delta patch eagerly as part of mount/hydration (ensure index stable) 2) modify warmup to operate on base+delta (apply virtualized offsets) 3) change sidecar format to include stable index that refers to final layout.
Liam: Ops prefers minimal extra steps during mount. Eager patching adds IO and CPU at load time, but gives deterministic warmup. Virtualized offsets are more complex in runtime.
Rosa: Can we make the exporter create a "postpatch.index" sidecar so warmup can use it without applying binary patch? It would be small and cheaper than full tensor patching.
kyle: That seems reasonable: exporter writes .final.index alongside .delta. Warmup reads final.index, prefetches ranges, but loader still defers applying delta until first byte needed. So we get correct warmup without full patch.
Yuki: Edge-case: if final.index references byte ranges that aren't contiguous in base file due to in-place transforms, prefetch will cause many tiny reads. Need to ensure final.index groups ranges by underlying file to reduce requests. Exporter should coalesce ranges.
Priya: Add heuristics for warmup: coalesce adjacent ranges up to 512KB, drop tiny nonessential ranges if warmup budget exceeded. Document tradeoffs.
Liam: Also need a header field to signal presence of delta-sidecar.final_index and whether final_index is authoritative for warmup. Propose header.delta_hotpath = "final_index"|"apply_eager"|"none".
Rosa: Backcompat: if missing delta_hotpath, default to legacy: stream-first. But warn in model-catalog and metric.
kyle: Security note: final_index must be authenticated (signed) or have checksum so runtime doesn't trust a tampered index that points to wrong offsets. Add header.final_index_checksum.
Yuki: Good call. And we should tag metrics: delta.hotpath_used=true/false and delta.patch_mode=eager/lazy/index.
Liam: Implementation plan: exporter change (write coalesced final.index + checksum), loader change (if delta_hotpath==final_index -> warmup uses final.index; if missing -> stream), canary test (deploy bundle with final.index and measure warmup latency).
Rosa: Ops ask: add deploy flag "allow_delta_sidecars" so Dedicated clusters can opt out until we've validated.
Priya: Timeline: I'll draft RFC today describing header semantics and index coalescing rules. kyle will prototype loader logic (PR end of week). Yuki will add canary telemetry. Rosa will coordinate ops flag gating.
ops-bot: Canary deployment scheduled: delta-hotpath-test -> projected runtime metrics toggled.
kyle: Quick sketch pseudocode for loader warmup path:
```python
meta = read_header(path)
if meta.get('delta_hotpath') == 'final_index' and exists(path + '.final.index'):
    idx = read_final_index(path + '.final.index')
    ranges = coalesce_ranges(idx, max_gap=64*1024, max_span=512*1024)
    prefetch(ranges)
else:
    stream_warmup()
```
Yuki: Add rollout criteria: 95th percentile warmup latency improvement > 30% and no increased IO error rate for 24h.
Rosa: Also ensure our e2e canary includes a variety of shard counts (1, 4, 16) and both on-NFS and S3 backends.
Liam: One more: for on-prem customers who patch models in place, we need an offline verification job to regenerate final.index after transforms. Document that in the private-deploy notes.
Priya: Agreed. RFC will also include migration checklist and deprecation window for bundles that rely on implicit final layout.
kyle: I'll add unit tests for coalescing logic and a small synthetic integration test that simulates sparse deltas.
Yuki: Great. Let's keep this lightweight first and iterate. If canary looks good, we'll formalize in model-catalog and docs.
Rosa: Thanks all. I'll open the ops ticket for gating flag and schedule a meeting if needed. :white_check_mark:
Liam: Thanks team, PRs & RFC links in this thread when ready.
